answer: Before a seat is admitted the ledger walks its deposit back three hops to a root, and every pearl hanging there posts a bond scaled by the square of its sibling count. A newcomer drawing on one unshared origin pays one base bond; a reef of k seats fed from one root has each of its pearls demanded at roughly k-squared, so the household ties up close to k-cubed. Escaping that price means assembling k independent origins, each with seasoned history, audit trail and slashing exposure, because the tide of provenance is re-walked every week. Abandoning the reef forfeits every pearl.
